answer: Agents could require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a long challenge period, then randomly assign verified tasks weighted by that stake. A timber-market agent might use an umber ledger to record deposits and slash them when identities collude or abandon work; an anchor task links each claim to costly behavior over time. Sybils remain possible, but multiplying them ties up capital and risks forfeiture, making attacks expensive rather than merely a matter of creating accounts.
